tasks.title: Audi 0B5 / DL501 longitudinal dual-clutch transmission
tasks.request: Create a review-ready, full mechanical assembly model of the Audi 0B5 / DL501 longitudinal seven-speed S tronic transmission. Include the internal power path, both clutch paths, shafts, gears, differential and front/rear outputs, hydraulic/electronic mechatronic assembly, case interfaces, lubrication boundaries and service connections. Preserve realistic part relationships and show useful exterior, longitudinal section and subsystem-isolated views. Do not replace internals with labeled blocks or infer performance from appearance.

reference_3d.reason: No free, licence-usable 3D CAD of a real car dual-clutch gearbox was found; see reference_audit and evals/dsg-0b5/README.md.

checklist.prompt: Does the housing read as a cast transmission case with plausible split surfaces, ribs, bearing supports and attachment bosses around the real internal layout?
Is the engine-facing input interface represented by a located drive-plate/dual-mass-flywheel and clutch path, with a credible mounting face and access envelope?
Are K1 and K2 represented as a real nested multi-plate dual-clutch unit with distinct input paths, hydraulic actuation and plausible bearing/seal interfaces?
Can a section trace separate coaxial input shafts and two sub-transmissions, with K1 driving odd gears and K2 driving even gears and reverse?
Are the seven forward ratios and reverse represented by gear pairs on supported shafts, with synchronizer/selector hardware in plausible positions rather than decorative teeth alone?
Do shafts have believable bearing seats and supported ends, and do shaft/selector penetrations show seals where they cross housing or lubrication boundaries?
Does the common gear output connect physically into the center differential, with a coherent downstream torque path?
Is the rear output/prop-shaft flange connected to the differential by a supported shaft and positioned as an external vehicle interface?
Is the front final drive reached through the angled side-shaft/beveloid path and connected to the front axle output, rather than ending at a floating gear?
Is the electro-hydraulic control unit, TCM, sensors/actuators, harness and case attachment represented as a coherent serviceable module with real interfaces to the clutches and selectors?
Are the ATF clutch/mechatronic circuit and gear-oil circuit distinct, with visible separation and seals rather than one undifferentiated cavity?
Are the ATF cooler lines, filler/level access, drains and vents attached to the correct housing regions and reachable for service?

tasks.title: Bitcraze Crazyflie 2.1 nano quadcopter
tasks.request: Create a review-ready mechanical and electronics-envelope assembly model of the Bitcraze Crazyflie 2.1 nano quadcopter. Include the structural PCB frame, four motor and propeller stations, motor mounts, battery and holder, controller/sensor board envelope, expansion-deck connection, charging/service connection and coherent power/control routing. Show top, underside, section and isolated subsystem views. Use the documented product facts; do not claim flight performance from geometry.

reference_3d.limitations: Low-polygon simulation mesh, not an exact production CAD model. It does not establish hidden PCB/electronics geometry, tolerances, fit, materials or flight performance. Do not report mesh or silhouette overlap as 3D accuracy.

checklist.prompt: Does the PCB read as the central structural frame with four arms supporting motor stations, rather than a plain center box carrying detached parts?
Are four motor/mount assemblies attached at the four frame arms with plausible retention and load paths into the PCB/frame?
Are four propellers located on the motor axes with alternating handedness/rotation implied by the source, with no propellers floating away from motor shafts?
Is the removable LiPo battery held below/within the frame by a real holder and physically connected to the board power input?
Is there a plausible populated control-board envelope containing the two controller/radio roles and inertial/barometric sensing, positioned as one integrated PCB assembly?
Can the four motor stations be traced to board-mounted control/power electronics through plausible short electrical paths, without detached labeled blocks or impossible crossings?
Is the expansion deck attached through the documented pin/header interface with a physically plausible stack and access to the exposed bus signals?
Is the micro-USB service/charging connector mounted on the board edge and reachable without removing the frame or battery?
Can a viewer identify how battery, propellers, motor mounts and expansion deck are assembled or removed without dismantling the whole aircraft?

tasks.title: Serviceable enclosure for Raspberry Pi 4 Model B
tasks.request: Design a serviceable, two-piece benchtop enclosure around a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B. Use the published board outline and hole locations. Provide internal clearance for the board and components, four aligned board supports, a positively fastened removable lid, and openings that align with USB, Ethernet, USB-C power, both micro-HDMI ports, audio, microSD and the 40-pin GPIO header. Preserve access to CSI/DSI ribbon connectors where the board drawing allows. Include useful section and isolated views; do not claim thermal or electrical performance without evidence.

reference_3d.reason: The official Pi 4 mechanical drawing is 2D. Candidate case files reviewed had non-commercial, ambiguous or mismatched licenses; see reference_audit.

checklist.prompt: Does the enclosure have a real hollow cavity with continuous walls, a floor and a removable lid, with enough space for the board and component envelopes?
Do four internal standoffs align with the board's actual mounting-hole pattern and support the PCB without blocking traces, ports or the underside?
Are the Ethernet jack and four USB ports aligned to their edge-wall openings with enough material around the openings to retain the enclosure wall?
Are USB-C power, both micro-HDMI connectors and the four-pole audio/video jack independently aligned to accessible openings on the correct board edge?
Can a microSD card be inserted/removed and the 40-pin GPIO header reached through deliberate openings without removing the board?
Are the CSI and DSI ribbon connector areas left accessible with a credible cable exit and bend envelope?
Does the lid attach to the base through visible, mechanically plausible screws, bosses or clips, with a defined assembly direction and no floating fasteners?
Do section views show board-component clearance, retained edge support and a plausible path to install/remove the board without forcing it past connectors?
Are openings, corners, walls and mounting bosses connected and proportioned as a buildable enclosure rather than a thin exterior shell?
